one: Simulate human society with agent-based models and generative agents, and run 'what if' experiments.
pos: Taught by Michael Bernstein and Noah Goodman, CS 222 spans social science, behavioral science, and generative AI. It moves from classical agent-based modeling to LLM-driven generative agents, discussing how to simulate individuals and societies, how to evaluate simulation fidelity, and the ethical issues involved.
topics: **Social simulation**: opinion spread, cooperation, public policy
**Ethics**: manipulation, privacy, the power of simulation
prereq: Python programming; AI (CS 221/224), human-centered design, or social psychology helps but is not required.
assess: Mainly a team project plus assignments/discussion. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: Computational social science, multi-agent systems, AI policy/ethics; anyone who wants to build social simulations or generative agents.
tips: Read Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023) and classic Schelling/NetLogo models first. Pay attention to reproducibility and ethical boundaries.
